scripts.radio:
Good evening, listener, and welcome to Kenya on Record. This week, our household budgets are absorbing another shock. Escalating conflicts in the Middle East have driven up global crude costs, and as always, the effect at our local fuel pump is immediate. When diesel and petrol rise, it is never just about motorists. Matatu fares creep up, farm produce costs more to transport to market, and the family shopping basket shrinks.

Away from the markets, there is quiet dignity in our history. Deep inside the Aberdare National Park, the Kenya Wildlife Service continues to preserve a historic mugumo tree once used by Mau Mau freedom fighters as an ingenious, clandestine postal drop. It stands as an enduring monument to the discipline and sacrifice that birthed our nation.

That legacy demands that we safeguard what belongs to the public today. As debates intensify over the sale of key state enterprises, we must hold government strictly to the law and its campaign pledges. National assets belong to the people of Kenya. Any disposal done without comprehensive public disclosure, independent valuations, and citizen participation violates both legal statutes and democratic trust.

Kwa ufupi: Kupanda kwa bei ya mafuta duniani kumezidisha gharama ya maisha na usafiri nchini. Huko Aberdare, mti wa mugumo uliotumiwa na Mau Mau unakumbusha umuhimu wa kulinda urithi wetu. Mwisho, uuzaji wowote wa mashirika ya umma lazima ufanyike kwa uwazi kamili na kufuata sheria bila kuficha chochote.
scripts.voice_note:
Habari zenu, this is Kenya on Record with your weekly accountability briefing. 

First, check your wallet: international crude prices spiked due to renewed conflicts in the Middle East, and the ripple effect has hit our pump prices. Expect matatu operators and food distributors to pass down the extra cost, so plan your weekly budget with care.

Second, keep your eyes on public property. The government is moving forward with plans to sell several state corporations. The law and past political promises are very clear: privatising public wealth requires open disclosure, parliamentary scrutiny, and public participation. Demand to see the valuation reports and buyer lists.

Finally, a point of national pride: the historic mugumo tree in the Aberdares, used as a secret message drop by the Mau Mau, remains protected. Our forebears guarded this country with their lives—let us guard its resources with our vigilance. Forward this to your group, and stay informed.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: Any sale of state corporations requires full public disclosure and public participation by law. Demand transparency before national assets are sold.
scripts.reels: Who actually owns Kenya's state corporations? You do. When the state moves to sell public assets, the law and campaign commitments require total transparency. No boardroom shortcuts, no undervalued disposals, and no hidden buyers. Every valuation and tender detail must be made public before a single asset changes hands. National wealth is not private property. Stay vigilant, ask the hard questions, and hold leadership to account.
